articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Dynasty Cheat Sheet, Printable Rankings for Redraft Leagues
articles.summary: The dynasty-league portion of the fantasy football community is forever looking forward.
articles.body:
The dynasty-league portion of the fantasy football community is forever looking forward.

So, while they're awaiting the opening of the 2026 NFL season like everyone else, they're also thinking about a big picture that extends well beyond the upcoming campaign.

For long-term rebuilders, that might be their lone focus. But even win-right-now contenders should devote some roster space to long-term lottery tickets, because it's never a good thing to let the cupboard run dry.

To help get you prepped for this season but also stocked for the long haul, we're providing both dynasty and redraft rankings while spotlighting a few sleepers with clear dynasty-league appeal.

Douglas, a third-round rookie out of Texas Tech, already seems primed to play a major role in Miami's offense. There are targets available in this offense—which could often find itself playing from behind—and Douglas seems as likely as anyone to command them. He had a buzzy training camp, and if that gets him on the runway for a strong rookie season, he could be a dynasty asset for a while.

The now Mike McDaniel-led Chargers' offense feels like one you'll want exposure to, and Harris could be a sneaky-significant role in it. If nothing else, his blocking should keep him on the field, and that in turn should give him a chance to showcase his talents as a dynamic pass-catcher. He can dazzle both as a vertical field-spacer and a yards-after-catch creator.

Johnson looks better on film than he does on the workout circuit, which helps explain why he fell to this year's fifth round despite rushing for 1,451 yards and 12 touchdowns at Nebraska last season. The Chiefs clearly aren't complaining; they already cleared Johnson's path to playing time by waiving veteran Emari Demercado, and they could have passing-down duties ready for Johnson and maybe a lot more should Kenneth Walker III miss any time.

articles.title: Father of Patrick Mahomes asks court to attend son's games amid probation for driving while intoxicated
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes Sr. filed a motion to leave Texas for seven Kansas City Chiefs games while on probation after a DWI guilty plea and violation.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes Sr., who is on probation after pleading guilty to driving while intoxicated, filed a motion to try to see his son, Patrick Mahomes, play this season. Mahomes Sr. filed the motion Friday in the 7th District Court in Tyler, Texas, according to FOX10. He requested permission to leave the state for seven of his son’s games in Kansas City, Missouri; Las Vegas, Nevada; and Cincinnati, Ohio, according to FOX10. In the motion, Mahomes Sr. acknowledges that to leave the state, he must submit to urinalysis testing both before and after he travels and notify a supervising officer each time he departs the state. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Mahomes Sr. pleaded guilty to driving while intoxicated in 2024 and was sentenced to five years of probation. He was arrested in February 2026 on charges of violating the terms of his probation after drinking alcohol, according to Smith County District Attorney Jacob Putman. The violation extended his probation by another two years. The motion Mahomes Sr. filed noted that he completed 16 weeks of outpatient treatment and 160 hours of community service. The motion also states that Mahomes Sr. has complied with all current probation conditions and is monitored by an ankle monitor, both of which can be verified by a Smith County community supervision officer. articles.title: Drake Maye Not Eyeing Revenge Game vs. Seahawks for Super Bowl 60 in Patriots' Season Opener
articles.summary: Drake Maye doesn't view the New England Patriots' season-opening clash with the Seattle Seahawks as an opportunity for revenge for the team's Super Bowl LX defeat.
articles.body:
Drake Maye doesn't view the New England Patriots' season-opening clash with the Seattle Seahawks as an opportunity for revenge for the team's Super Bowl LX defeat.

"They won the big one," Maye said Saturday, per MassLive's Mark Daniels .

Seattle was able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy by wrapping up a 29-13 win over New England in last season's Super Bowl matchup.

5 Fantasy Football League Winners for 2026 NFL Season

Buzz: Baker Frustrated with Bucs Talks 😠

Maye finished 27-of-43 for 295 yards and two touchdowns compared to two interceptions in the contest. He also lost a fumble.

It was a tough end to a promising overall season from the Patriots, as their deep playoff run came after a 2024 campaign in which they compiled a 4-13 record.

Maye was particularly stellar last year, finishing No. 2 in MVP voting and earning a Second Team All-Pro nod.

He completed 72.0 percent of his passes for 4,394 yards and 31 touchdowns while getting picked off just eight times. Maye's 77.1 QBR ranked No. 1 among 28 qualified quarterbacks, via ESPN .

The Patriots have their sights set on putting together another strong year in 2026 following a busy offseason. They made several additions on offense, signing wide receiver Romeo Doubs and guard Alijah Vera-Tucker in free agency.

They also acquired three-time Pro Bowl receiver A.J. Brown in a blockbuster trade with the Philadelphia Eagles on June 1.

Although the Seahawks didn't make any major external offseason additions and lost running back Kenneth Walker III in free agency, they're still a threat to win consecutive Super Bowl titles.

After all, they still boast an offense headlined by reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba and a defense that ranked No. 1 in the NFL by allowing a mere 17.2 points per game last season.

Even if a Patriots win over Seattle in Week 1 won't make up for their Super Bowl loss, it would help them open the year with plenty of momentum.

Kickoff between New England and Seattle is on Wednesday at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Somehow, the Miami Hurricanes have done it again with yet another Heisman-level quarterback
articles.summary: Darian Mensah's dominant debut at Miami continues a stunning pattern as Mario Cristobal lands yet another elite transfer portal quarterback.
articles.body: I remember it like it was yesterday. January 13, 2024. I was at a friend's birthday party with a group of fans representing each of the "Big 3" Florida schools (Miami, Florida, and Florida State). Being a Gator fan, I was relishing in joining my fellow Florida fanatics and Seminole supporters mocking the Miami contingent that they had whiffed on all their quarterback targets in the transfer portal. ACC SUPREMACY: IS IT REALLY THE MIAMI HURRICANES VERSUS THE FIELD FOR THE 2026 SEASON? As we laughed and reveled in their misery, a notification flashed across everyone's phone screen that changed the tide of the night in favor of the Canes fans. "BREAKING: Cam Ward, the ex-Washington State QB, heading to Miami." ONE OF THESE EIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS WILL BE HOISTING THE NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP TROPHY IN 2026 The Hurricanes had found their guy, but after a Heisman-level season in 2024, their one year rental was off to the NFL Draft. So Miami's rivals fired up the trolls once again, and towards the end of the portal period, it looked like the Hurricanes were going to have to eat crow. That is, until they plucked Georgia quarterback Carson Beck from the ranks of the NFL Draft. Then the Canes rode another late transfer pickup to within a quarter of winning the national championship. So when Miami and Mario Cristobal were without a signal caller heading into the teeth of the offseason, we all knew better than to gloat. And that proved to be the right decision, as the Canes once again persuaded an NFL Draft hopeful - this time Duke transfer Darian Mensah - to hop in the boat in Coral Gables. UCLA QUARTERBACK ATTEMPTS TO EXPLOIT LOOPHOLE IN TRANSFER PORTAL WINDOW WITH UNIQUE TACTIC Mensah was given a king's ransom to make his way down to South Florida, and so far, though it's only been one game, that investment is looking to be paying dividends. I think I speak for the rest of college football when I ask: how do the Canes keep doing this? COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S AP TOP 25 IS OUT: WHO’S OVERRATED, UNDERRATED AND FLAT-OUT SNUBBED? I'm reminded of the famous scene from "Breaking Bad," when Aaron Paul's character screams "HE CAN'T KEEP GETTING AWAY WITH IT!" Granted, Miami played a Stanford team that was missing half its roster due to injury and probably isn't much to write home about even when fully healthy. But those numbers would look good in a 7-on-7 scrimmage, let alone in a conference game on the road three time zones from home. Mensah looked as good as the numbers suggested, too, ripping NFL-level throws and distributing the ball to his myriad playmakers, namely wide receiver Malachi Toney. Somehow, some way, Cristobal and the Canes have another quarterback who can realistically win the Heisman trophy and lead them on a deep Playoff run. The schedule for Miami won't offer a ton of resistance either; there will be far more Stanford-level teams than Playoff-caliber ones. When you combine all that and Mensah's skill with the weapons he's been surrounded with (not to mention elite offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson), the Hurricanes might be here to stay.
